# A Distribution Plan for a Product the Platforms Restrict: One Fintech Company, Ninety Days.

Source: https://lowob.com/research/restricted-category-distribution-worked-example/
Publisher: lowob (https://lowob.com)
Published: 2026-09-01 · Updated: 2026-11-16
Function: Distribution

> Summary: A composite consumer fintech with two rejected ad accounts and an unspent budget works through the method over ninety days: a band map built from the platforms' own policies, a one-week test of three open channels with written thresholds, one channel built properly, and the rest added in proportion. No channel ends above half of funded accounts, and nothing depended on getting past a review.

This is the restricted-category method applied to one composite company: a consumer fintech app with a yield-bearing account through a partner bank, two ad accounts rejected and a budget sitting unspent. Over ninety days it maps the bands from the platforms' own policies, spends $14,000 testing three open channels against written thresholds, builds the one that read, and adds the rest in proportion. At day ninety no channel carries more than half of funded accounts, finance can reconcile the cost per funded account, and nothing required getting past a review.

Abstract frameworks are easy to nod at. This is what the method looks like on one company.

Illustrative example: the company

Illustrative: a composite built from patterns across engagements. No figure below is a client result.

## Weeks one and two: the map and the sounding

The first job is to write down where the company cannot be seen, from each platform's own published policy, with the date it was read.

| Channel | What the policy requires | Band at week one |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Meta | Financial ads to US audiences run in a special ad category: fixed age range, no gender targeting, minimum location radius, no lookalike audiences. Documentation the company can supply, with no defined review timeline | Restricted, paperwork filed |
| Google Ads | Financial services verification in the locations that require it, with licences and registration numbers; physical address and fees disclosed on the page | Restricted, paperwork filed |
| TikTok | Local licensing, disclosures and 18+ targeting; in the company's main market the product sits in a category needing pre-approval it cannot yet obtain | Closed for now |
| Programmatic exchanges | Carry the category against the company's own audience definitions | Open |
| Affiliate networks | At least one network carries the category | Open |
| Creators | Carry it with disclosure and compliant claims | Open |
| Owned email and content | No platform approval | Open |

So: two channels in the restricted band with paperwork filed and nothing forecast, one closed for now, and four open.

The second job is a one-week measurement across three of the open channels, each with a written question.

| Channel | Written question | Threshold set in advance |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Affiliate | Can comparison and personal-finance publishers produce funded accounts below $100 each on a bounty model, with the company's own tracking confirming the funding event? | Cost per funded account under $100 |
| Creators | Can mid-tier personal-finance creators, on a cost-per-funded-account basis and with pre-approved claims, produce at least forty funded accounts in a week? | 40 funded accounts |
| Programmatic | Against an audience the company defines, with a real-CPM standard and a rejection rule, can display and short video produce installs that fund at a rate comparable to organic? | Funding rate close to organic |

$14,000 across the three. Tracking in the company's own analytics. A decision written in advance for each. [Campaign testing that reaches a decision](https://lowob.com/research/campaign-testing-that-reaches-a-decision/) explains why the decision is written before the test, and why small B2B and fintech volumes should be read as direction rather than proof.

## Week two's result

Affiliate read. Eleven publishers recruited by hand, sixty-three funded accounts confirmed, a cost per funded account of $71, no coupon partners admitted. For context, WordStream's 2026 search benchmarks put the average Google Ads cost per lead in finance and insurance at $74.44. A lead is not a funded account, so the comparison flatters search rather than affiliate; the affiliate figure is for the outcome that matters.

Creators read partially: strong cost per account from three of the eight, nothing from the rest. Programmatic did not read: installs were cheap, funding was poor, and the rejection rate on the initial buy was near zero, which explained the cheap installs.

The decision, per the written thresholds: build the affiliate programme now, expand the three creators into a structured programme, and hold programmatic until a proper desk with inventory standards can be stood up.

> None of it required getting past a review. All of it required knowing where the answer was already yes.

## Weeks three to eight: build the thing that read

The affiliate programme gets terms: a bounty on funded accounts above a minimum balance, a thirty-day cookie, a validation period long enough to catch reversals, no brand bidding, no scraped codes, coupon partners tiered at a lower rate and capped. It is placed on one network that carries the category, with a direct platform for the hand-recruited publishers. Forty partners are recruited in six weeks, each with creative, an FAQ and a compliance-approved claims sheet. [Referral partners without leakage](https://lowob.com/research/referral-partners-without-leakage/) and our piece on [affiliate programmes that do not pay for coupon leaks](https://lowob.com/research/affiliate-program-asset-or-coupon-leak/) cover each term.

The creator programme gets a brief, disclosure language, per-creator tracking and cost-per-funded-account terms. The three that converted recruit the next tier. The disclosure language follows the US Federal Trade Commission's 2023 Endorsement Guides, which added a definition of "clear and conspicuous" and warned that a platform's built-in disclosure tool might not be adequate. The guides also set out the potential liability of advertisers as well as endorsers, which is why the claims sheet is the company's, not the creator's.

Owned channels get the neglected fix: every partner and creator link lands on a page that asks for an email, and the list gets a fortnightly message compliance has reviewed.

## Weeks nine to thirteen: add the desk

With affiliate and creators producing, programmatic is revisited under proper terms: a flat fee per account, an inclusion list, a verification standard, a rejection rule that discards inventory failing it, and a real-CPM report. The buy is optimised to funded accounts, not installs. It reads, at a higher cost per outcome than affiliate, and is kept at a size that does not crowd the channel that works. Our piece on [programmatic numbers you can trust](https://lowob.com/research/programmatic-media-numbers-you-can-trust/) covers the standard.

The Meta approval arrives in week eleven. It is added as a fourth channel, capped, and its outcomes compared with the others on incrementality rather than on its own attribution. The special ad category limits matter here: without lookalikes or detailed demographic targeting, Meta behaves less like a precision tool and more like broad reach, which is another reason to judge it against a holdout. [Attribution vs incrementality](https://lowob.com/research/attribution-vs-incrementality/) covers the method.

## What the numbers had to show

| Measure at day ninety | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Share of funded accounts by channel | Affiliate about half; creators about a quarter; programmatic and Meta the rest |
| Largest channel share | No channel above half |
| Largest partner share | No partner above a third of affiliate outcomes |
| Cost per funded account | A real figure finance can reconcile, by channel |
| Owned audience | An email list that did not exist in week one |
| Band map | A written record of which channels are closed and why |

At no point did the company attempt to disguise its category or open a replacement account. Google's circumventing systems policy suspends accounts for that on detection, without warning and permanently. The plan would have been worth less than the risk.

A restricted-category distribution plan is a map, a week of cheap measurement, one channel built properly, and the rest added in proportion. The approvals are a bonus, never the foundation.

## lowob takeaways

- **Map from the platforms' own pages.** Record the band, the requirement and the date for every channel.
- **Write the threshold before the test.** Each open channel answers one question with a number set in advance.
- **Build the channel that read, with terms.** Bounties on funded accounts, validation periods and coupon caps.
- **Add late approvals capped.** Judge them on incrementality against the channels already working.
- **End with no channel above half.** The map, the list and a reconciled cost per funded account are the assets.

## Common questions

### How do you build a distribution plan for a fintech the ad platforms restrict?

Map every channel as open, restricted or closed from the platforms' own policies, test two or three open channels for a week against written thresholds, build the one that reads properly, and file restricted applications with nothing forecast against them.

### What is a good cost per funded account for a fintech affiliate programme?

It depends on account value and retention. Set the threshold from your own unit economics before testing; in this composite it was under $100, and the programme read at $71.

### How should affiliate terms for a fintech be structured?

Pay a bounty on funded accounts above a minimum balance, with a validation period that catches reversals, no brand bidding, no scraped codes, and coupon partners tiered lower and capped.

### What changes when a Meta financial ad approval finally arrives?

Add it as a capped channel and compare it with the others on incrementality. For US audiences it runs in a special ad category without lookalikes, so judge it against a holdout rather than its own attribution.
